Study method details: Single-patient case report with systematic reagent/analyser troubleshooting: the same patient sample was run on multiple analysers and with multiple PT reagents, assisted by the manufacturer's application specialist; PT mixing test with normal pooled plasma showed non-correction (Rosner Index 39, where >=15 indicates an inhibitor); factor VII antigen 78.4% (reference 50-129%) with no FVII inhibitor detected, excluding factor deficiency (pp. 2-4)
Additional sources of bias: n = 1, so no generalisable magnitude; the patient was receiving rivaroxaban at the time of the earliest samples and enoxaparin later, both of which can themselves prolong the PT (the authors discuss rivaroxaban-induced PT prolongation explicitly); LA testing was performed while the patient was on low-molecular-weight heparin without concurrent anti-Xa levels, contrary to ISTH guidance; stage 3 chronic kidney disease and thrombocytopenia present; some comparisons are across different dates rather than strictly paired; patient lost to follow-up after 1 year
Notes: Resolution of the case: after switching to a tissue-derived thromboplastin the INR became usable for warfarin monitoring in the same LA-positive patient. On 12 May 2022 the patient was on warfarin (dose not stated on this date). Off warfarin (2 March 2022) the same LA-positive plasma gave INR 1.2 with STA-NeoPTimal versus INR 3.8-8.5 with Dade Innovin a few weeks earlier - the practical demonstration of reagent-dependent LA interference. Direction ↔ reflects the authors' statement that "LA does not seriously interfere with PT measurement with this system" and "Neoptimal was not as sensitive to LA as the Siemens Dade Innovin" (p. 4). No paired same-sample LA-free baseline is printed for these dates, so the calculated columns are the missing literal.
